newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi falls after poor half year results.
newsitem.headline: Sappi falls after poor half year results.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Sappi Ltd fell 2.00 rand to 39.00 rand at the start of trading on Monday after the paper and pulp producer announced a dive in half year earnings.
Earlier the firm posted six month earnings per share of 16 cents, down from 215 cents last time, and at the bottom end of a range of analysts' expectations of 10 to 40 cents.
The firm also held its dividend.
"They're a pretty poor set of results and the dividend news is certainly hitting the shares," one dealer said.
The firm has been hit by low prices in the notoriously cyclical industry which have offset a relatively healthy demand for pulp.
However, the group, whilst admitting full year profits will be down on last year, does see hopes for a recovery in the second half.
"Producer stocks have shown a decline in recent months and price increases have been announced by most of the major suppliers effective May, 1997," the firm said in a statement.
Sappi added that the price increases seemed to have been accepted by the market.
